newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - March 25.

text.p: The following stories were reported in Tuesday's electronic version of The Wall Street Journal:
* Stocks and bonds rose amid expectations the U.S. Federal Reserve will boost interest rates one quarter of a percentage point today.
* Philip Morris said James Kilts, executive vice president of worldwide foods, resigned. He led a two-year turnaround at the company's Kraft Foods unit.
* The Equal Employment Opportunity Commission plans to join a lawsuit alleging Home Depot discriminated against women in terms of promotions, raises and some jobs.
* Germany's Krupp and Thyssen agreed to merge their steel operations.
* Oxford Health shifted strategy by deciding to coordinate care for patients with chronic or expensive medical problems through specialists instead of primary-care doctors.
* The Supreme Court will decide how broadly General Motors can enforce a settlement agreement limiting a former employee's rights to testify against the company in product-liability cases.
* NASD is investigating Dean Witter to see if brokers told clients of investment risks when selling a $2 billion bond fund series.
* Canada's Avenor plans to complete its previously-announced acquisition of Repap, saying it turned down a merger proposal from Domtar.
* Internet book seller Amazon.com filed for an initial public offering valuing the company at almost $300 million.
* Lehman Brothers reported strong quarterly profit results.
* Reed-Elsevier agreed to pay $320 million to buy U.S. scientific-information company MDL Information.
* IBM's John Whiteside is leaving to head an electronic-commerce joint venture owned by Andersen Consulting and BBN.
* Motorola is seen winning a cellular telephone pact from a group of Japanese cellular telephone providers.
* Atlantic Richfield said it would give up its 49.9 percent stake in Lyondell Petrochemical and sees a $300 million after-tax gain.
* Heard on the street: Yesterday's flight from technology is more bad news for networking companies, which were among the first to be hit by worries about too-high valuations and slowing growth.

* Credit markets: Bond prices advanced yesterday in restless trading as investors focused on today's all-important meeting of the Federal Reserve's interest rate setting panel, the Federal Open Market Committee.
